About.title: About Me
About.intro:
Hi, I'm a sophomore majoring in CS at NCUE and the <highlight>Lead of GDGoC NCUE</highlight>!
I'm passionate about community involvement and love the energy of <highlight>working together towards a shared goal</highlight>.
Driven by the desire to make campus life easier with code, I took the initiative to <highlight>develop and maintain systems</highlight> for the Student Assistance Division, Campus Security Center, Career Center, and the Student Association.
I also believe that <highlight>"output is the best input."</highlight> I enjoy organizing what I’ve learned into structured technical articles to help others get up to speed faster. Recently, I've been fascinated by <highlight>Hardware Security and Cryptography</highlight> and am currently diving deep into these fields XD.
About.researchTitle: Design of a High-Stability PUF-Based Post-Quantum Key Generation System Based on FPGA XADC Environmental Sensing Mechanism
About.researchDesc: Addressing the threat of quantum computing to current encryption standards, this research proposes an <highlight>active hardware root-of-trust architecture</highlight> integrating environmental sensing to provide high-entropy keys for <highlight>Post-Quantum Cryptography (e.g., NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM)</highlight>. Traditional <highlight>Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs)</highlight> suffer from instability due to <highlight>PVT variations</highlight>, while standard passive Error Correcting Codes (ECC) consume excessive FPGA resources. To overcome these bottlenecks, this system utilizes the <highlight>FPGA's built-in XADC</highlight> for real-time environmental monitoring. By implementing a <highlight>closed-loop feedback mechanism</highlight> to dynamically adjust <highlight>Tunable Delay Lines (TDL)</highlight>, the architecture actively compensates for environmental drifts at the physical layer. The design significantly reduces bit error rates and <highlight>minimizes logic resource consumption</highlight> by eliminating heavy ECC requirements, delivering a robust and efficient post-quantum key generation solution tailored for <highlight>resource-constrained IoT edge devices</highlight>.

pqc.title: PQC Standards & Hardware Security
pqc.desc: Addressing post-quantum threats, this article details the NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) standard and the mathematical foundations of Lattice-based Cryptography. It focuses on critical security elements in FPGA implementation, including utilizing PUF (Physical Unclonable Functions) as high-entropy sources for Hardware Root of Trust (HRoT), and low-level circuit design strategies to mitigate micro-probing and Side-Channel Attacks (SCA).

cv.title: Computer Vision Algorithms & Applications
cv.desc: Explores the mathematical foundations and core operators of digital image processing. Starting with spatial domain filtering, it analyzes denoising techniques like Gaussian Smoothing and Median Filtering, followed by the implementation of Edge Detection algorithms such as Sobel and Canny. The article further examines morphological operations (e.g., Erosion, Dilation) for image segmentation, bridging these concepts to feature extraction principles in modern Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs).

docker.title: Docker Containers & Deployment
docker.desc: Addressing the "it works on my machine" dilemma, this article focuses on packaging applications and dependencies using containerization. It covers Dockerfile optimization and multi-stage builds, exploring how to integrate containers into CI/CD pipelines for Microservices architectures. The goal is to achieve automated testing and deployment, enhancing software delivery stability and scalability.
